title: India Condemns Karak Church Attack as Jordan Raises Death Toll to Eight
excerpt: New Delhi called the funeral shooting heinous and cowardly and stood with Jordan, as a critically injured victim died and 26 people remained in hospital.
body:
• India on Saturday condemned the October 23 church funeral attack in Karak, Jordan, as heinous and cowardly, and reaffirmed its commitment to fighting terrorism in all forms.
  • The death toll has risen to eight, Jordan's health minister said, after a critically injured victim died; 34 people were injured and 26 remained in hospital.
  • External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said he was deeply shocked and that India stands firmly with Jordan's government and people.
  • Our earlier report covered the attack and the US Embassy security alert: Seven Killed in Attack on Church Funeral in Jordan's Karak.

India on Saturday strongly condemned the shooting attack on a church funeral in Jordan's Karak governorate, calling it heinous and cowardly, and said it stands firmly with the government and people of Jordan. The statement from the Ministry of External Affairs came as Jordanian authorities raised the death toll from the October 23 attack to eight.

"India unequivocally condemns the heinous attack at a Church in Karak, Jordan, which resulted in the tragic loss of several innocent lives and injuries to many others. We extend our heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and wish a swift recovery to those injured in this cowardly attack," the MEA said, in a statement carried by IANS via India Tribune. "India stands firmly with the Government and the friendly people of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan in this difficult hour. We also reaffirm our strong commitment to the fight against terrorism in all its forms and manifestations."

"Deeply shocked at the heinous attack at a Church in Karak, Jordan yesterday, which resulted in the tragic loss of several innocent lives and injuries to many others."

— S. Jaishankar, External Affairs Minister, on X

Toll rises to eight dead, 34 injured

Gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Hammoud village in Karak, Jordan's southern governorate, on Friday, October 23. Jordan's Public Security Directorate initially reported seven people killed and 34 injured, and said the attack was carried out by unidentified individuals, with investigations proceeding intensively.

On Saturday, Health Minister Ibrahim al-Bdour confirmed the toll had risen to eight after a critically injured victim died, according to The CSR Journal. Twenty-six people remained in hospital, one of them in critical condition. Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya characterised the shooting as a terrorist act and said security forces were pursuing those responsible.

Jordan and the world respond

King Abdullah II termed the incident a terrorist attack and vowed the harshest retaliation. Prime Minister Jafar Hassan was to chair a meeting in Karak to oversee the official response, the government communication minister announced. ANI's account via LatestLY noted the same MEA language of zero tolerance for terrorism.

India's response follows a familiar pattern in its West Asia diplomacy: immediate, unambiguous condemnation, solidarity with the host government, and no speculation about the perpetrators before Jordan's investigation concludes. No group had claimed responsibility as of Saturday.

What to watch

Jordanian security services say the hunt for the attackers is continuing, and the investigation will determine whether the cell acted alone or had wider links. For Indian nationals in Jordan, the earlier US Embassy alert and heightened security posture around public places remain in effect. Further official updates are expected from Amman on the condition of the hospitalised and on any arrests.
